'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Operation Allies Refuge]]
***Seven people are killed during a [[stampede]] at the airport in [[Kabul]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-fire-air-control-crowd-kabul-airport-2021-08-22/ (Reuters)]
***[[United States Army]] [[Major general (United States)|major general]] [[William D. Taylor (general)|William D. Taylor]] announces that the [[United States]] has evacuated 17,000 people, including 2,500 [[Americans]], in the past few weeks. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/08/21/us-says-2500-americans-evacuated-from-kabul-in-past-week.html (CNBC)]
***The U.S. and [[Germany]] both issue advisories warning nationals not to travel to the [[Hamid Karzai International Airport]] in [[Kabul]] almost a week after the Taliban took control. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/taliban-vow-be-accountable-probe-reports-reprisals-afghanistan-2021-08-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Northern Chad]]
**[[Chad]] recalls half of its 1,200 troops in the tri-border area of [[Mali]], [[Burkina Faso]] and [[Niger]]. The decision notified to the coalition by Chadian military was explained as part of a plan to deploy troops elsewhere, where Chad is currently facing other conflicts. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/chad-halve-its-troops-fighting-sahel-militants-spokesperson-says-2021-08-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
*****[[New South Wales]] reports a record of 825 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, which is the highest number reported by any [[States and territories of Australia|state or territory]] since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-08-21/nsw-records-825-covid-cases-three-deaths/100396208  (ABC News Australia)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
*****Regional [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] re-enters a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] as COVID-19 infections spread from an ongoing cluster in [[Melbourne]]. [https://www.theage.com.au/national/victoria/victoria-s-new-restrictions-all-the-changes-you-need-to-know-20210821-p58kov.html?utm_medium=Social&utm_source=Facebook&fbclid=IwAR1BHvZxQz-S86E_ZMLXaBFeMb6GU_4FpF3NsMB0Mc710ESYPFCL5y2ZAIw#Echobox=1629511222-1 (''The Age'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] reports 21 new community transmitted cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total since April 2020. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/aug/21/this-isnt-surprising-jacinda-ardern-warns-new-zealanders-to-remain-calm-as-covid-cases-rise (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Palau]]
****[[Palau]] reports their first cases of COVID-19 in two people who travelled from [[Guam]] and were placed in [[quarantine]] with their known contacts. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210821-palau-loses-virus-free-status-with-first-covid-cases (France 24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] receives a shipment of 781,440 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] donated by [[Japan]]. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/08/21/bangladesh-gets-7-81-440-doses-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-from-japan (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brunei]]
****[[Brunei]] extends its nationwide partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for two weeks until September 4 amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/brunei-extends-partial-lockdown-amid-daily-spike-of-over-100-covid-19-cases (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 11,321 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 336,707. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/08/22/vietnam-confirms-record-daily-covid-19-cases-for-three-consecutive-days (''The Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
***[[Morocco]] surpasses 800,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.mapnews.ma/en/actualites/general/morocco-reports-6513-new-cases-over-past-24-hours (MAP News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of Afghanistan]]
**The [[European Union]] says that there will be "no recognition, no political talks" with the [[Taliban]]. [[President of the European Commission|European Commission president]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] says that the EU will "measure the Taliban by their deeds and actions" before engaging in any recognition. Von der Leyen also announced an increase in humanitarian aid to Afghanistan. [https://www.reuters.com/world/eu-says-no-recognition-taliban-no-political-talks-2021-08-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Taliban offensive]], [[LGBT rights in Afghanistan]], [[Persecution of homosexuals]]
**Afghan-American [[LGBT rights]] activist [[Nemat Sadat]] says that [[gay]] Afghans are facing death under the [[Taliban]], as a 21-year-old man from [[Balkh Province]] says that he is trying to [[seek asylum]] and thinks that he may never see his boyfriend again. Another gay man from [[Kabul]] who worked for the [[United Nations]] described the current situation for [[homosexual]]s as a "nightmare". [https://uk.news.yahoo.com/men-afghanistans-secret-gay-community-084957015.html (Yahoo! News)]
*Former president of Bolivia [[Jeanine Áñez]] cuts her arm while in jail in what was allegedly a suicide attempt. [https://elcomercio.pe/mundo/latinoamerica/bolivia-expresidenta-jeanine-anez-intenta-suicidarse-pero-es-atendida-por-medicos-noticia/ (''El Comercio'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/former-bolivian-president-anez-harmed-herself-while-jail-lawyer-2021-08-21/ (Reuters)]
